I have farmed this land in Quzhou for thirty years. I know what the soil needs, what the weather does, and what prices have looked like. My children help some seasons but they also work in town, so I have to be realistic about labor.

My 10.1 mu is split: about 6 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation — wheat in winter, maize right after harvest in summer on the same ground. That rotation is what I know best and it gives two harvests a year. The other 4.1 mu I put into cotton. Cotton is harder work but it brings in cash.

**Wheat**: I plant in mid-October. I use the improved variety I have been using for several years — it yields well here and I trust it. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and then chase with urea at jointing. In Quzhou the winters are dry, so I water three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at grain fill. Two pesticide passes — one for aphids in spring, one for disease. Rotary tillage before planting.

**Maize**: Goes in right after wheat harvest in June. No time for tillage so I drill it direct. I use a hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or something similar from the county seed station, same as most years. Summer rains help but I usually irrigate twice. Fertilize at planting and top-dress at tasseling. Pests need two spray rounds.

**Cotton**: Spring planting, April. I use hybrid Bt cotton — has cut down on the bollworm spraying a lot compared to the old days, but I still spray several times for other insects. Cotton needs more irrigation than grain crops, especially August when it flowers and bolls. I do rotary tillage to prepare the bed properly. It is the most labor-intensive but we manage.
